evidence: CONFIRMED_CONTENT: NavierStokes.AxisOperators.regularInverse, NavierStokes/AxisOperators.lean:470, defines J_r by the coefficient rule inverseScale, i.e. by (B.5). AxisEvaluationAlgebra.lean:478 (ODE), :148 (G(0)=0) and AxisEvaluation.lean:260 (smooth on strip I 20) prove that this element is a regular solution. Nothing states that a regular solution is this element.

ATTRIBUTION_GAP: AxisOperators.lean:330 (product ≤ 64), :479 (average ≤ 1), :482 (primitive ≤ 80), :485 (regularInverse ≤ 80), :488 (parameterPrimitive ≤ 80/ε), :491 (mulY ≤ 80), :719/:725/:731 ((B.6) and its two derivative-omitted variants), AxisInverseFactors.lean:210/:253 (extra factors). No declaration conjoins them; a grep of NavierStokes/ for 'Lemma B|B\.5|B\.6' finds no citing docstring, the only tag being 'GAX.2' at AxisCoefficientSpace.lean:428.

ATTRIBUTION_GAP: NavierStokes.AxisOperators.norm_inverseMixed_le, NavierStokes/AxisOperators.lean:719, and NavierStokes.AxisOperators.norm_average_le, :479; the omitted-derivative variants are stated outright at :725 and :731, the averaged one is not. CONVENTION: NavierStokes.AxisWeightEstimates.productWeightSum_le, NavierStokes/AxisWeightEstimates.lean:298, bounds the weight convolution by 64·weight ε n m via squareDecay_convolution_le (:125), which gives 8 per index where (B.7) gives 8∑_{i≥1}i^{-2} =: C_sq ≈ 13.16. The docstring at :297 calls 64 'the manuscript's uniform algebra constant', which for this manuscript it is not.

Read p. 145 and p. 146 and the five Axis* files. The space is literal: weight is 𝔞_{αβ}, axisSpace_norm_le_iff is ‖·‖_ρ. Every boundedness clause is stated, each for every r ≥ 1 and with the paper's own shift constants 80, 80/ρ, 1 from (B.9)-(B.10); (B.6) and both derivative-omitted variants carry an explicit C_ρ = 5120/ρ, and the extra-factor clause is stated for a whole list. Those clauses conjoin by logic alone. What does not is the first sentence of (B.5): Lean defines J_r by (B.5) and proves it is a regular solution, while the paper asserts the regular solution has those coefficients. The converse needs an ODE uniqueness argument stated nowhere, so partial/DELTA, with the gap low by consequence.

findings.summary: Lemma B.1 defines J_ν as *the* smooth solution of YG_YY+νG_Y=F with G(0)=0 and asserts its coefficients are (B.5). Lean defines J_r by (B.5) and proves the converse direction only; no declaration states that these properties determine G.

No declaration states Lemma B.1, and none cites it. Its boundedness clauses are stated faithfully one at a time across about fifteen declarations in five files, so the pairing is inferred rather than declared.
The (B.6) variant with F replaced by A_X(F) has no declaration of its own, unlike the two derivative-omitted variants. It is the one-line composite of norm_inverseMixed_le with norm_average_le.
Lean's algebra constant is 64; the paper's proof route gives C_sq² = (8·π²/6)² ≈ 173. Lemma B.1 and (B.6) name no constant, so Lean's 64 and 5120/ε are its own sharper numbers, not the manuscript's.
